briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Grinds On, But Relief Signals Multiply — While DC and the FDA Hand Cannabis and Psychedelics Real Wins
briefs.top: Michigan's wholesale tax fight is heading to a September trial and now both major gubernatorial nominees are promising repeal, while operators who restructure supplier deals are proving the 24% hit is survivable. Nationally, momentum keeps building: Congress just bought hemp THC products a reprieve, the DEA rescheduling process is moving, and Compass Pathways' psilocybin drug is racing toward an FDA decision.

local.text: Michigan GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a 'Freedom Agenda' plank pledging to repeal or roll back the 24% wholesale cannabis tax, arguing it 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections' — giving operators a real electoral path to relief in November.

Democratic candidate Chris Swanson has also vowed to repeal the tax if elected, calling it 'not fair and equitable' to an industry that provides jobs — meaning cannabis relief is now bipartisan campaign currency heading into the general election.

Upper Michigan multi-store operator Rize has managed to sustain growth despite the wholesale tax by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers, splitting the tax burden rather than absorbing it alone — a playbook other operators can copy.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is pushing the retail format forward, targeting a fall opening for a dispensary paired with a full-service restaurant — a hospitality-forward buildout further than most Michigan operators have gone.

Jars Cannabis won removal of a Flock surveillance camera near its Madison Heights location, a local regulatory win for retailers even as the industry's second constitutional challenge to the 24% tax — over 'tax pyramiding' that inflates the effective sales-tax rate — heads toward a September trial that could finally deliver a court-ordered fix.

national.text: The DEA's marijuana rescheduling hearings wrapped by mid-July, and the agency is now sending Colorado medical cannabis businesses a 26-question protections application tied to the Trump administration's rescheduling push — a sign the process is moving from hearings into real implementation.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin drug COMP360 keeps clearing hurdles: the FDA granted a rolling NDA review and awarded it a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for treatment-resistant depression, putting the first-ever psilocybin therapy on track for a Q4 2026 submission.

Congress just gave the hemp industry breathing room: the House passed a 370-48 vote on September 1 to delay the federal hemp THC recriminalization from November 12 to December 11, 2026, and the bill now heads to Trump's desk for an expected signature.

The FDA finalized its clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and set a September 14 public hearing on psychedelic therapeutic use — analysts called it 'a more supportive regulatory environment that could reduce regulatory risk for psychedelic drug developers' including Compass, Atai, Cybin and GH Research.

Consolidation is accelerating as stronger operators expand: Grown Rogue is acquiring PharmaCann's New York license, cultivation facility and four dispensaries in a joint venture, while distressed assets from a defaulted Justice Grown loan are heading to a September court hearing and auction — creating fresh buying opportunities for well-capitalized multistate operators.
